newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Western Metals half-yr profit falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Western Metals half-yr profit falls.

text.p: Zinc/lead miner Western Metals Ltd said on Thursday its after-tax profit for the half-year to December 31 fell to A$1.28 million from A$2.48 million in the previous corresponding period.

The result was achieved despite a period of flat zinc prices and an appreciating Australian dollar against the U.S. dollar, the company said. Falling lead prices and high treatment charges for both lead and zinc were contributing factors, it said.
Managing director Rod Webster said it was pleasing that the company had been able to remain profitable.
The company remained confident the improving outlook for the second half would allow a dividend to be paid for the full 1996/97 financial year, he said.

The company was debt-free and poised to take advantage of rapidly improving market conditions, Webster said. Zinc prices had increased by more than 10 percent since the close of the half-year and the Australian dollar had dropped, he said.

The company was taking advantage of the falling Australian dollar and had built up a strong foreign exchange hedged position with about US$100 million at a weighted average of US$0.777 cents, he said.

It was planned to increase this level of protection to ensure the company gained the full benefit of a rising zinc price without the offsetting effect of an appreciating Australian dollar, Webster said.
The company would begin regional exploration on tenements surrounding existing mining leases in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, he said.
Over the last two years Western Metals had spent more than A$1 million collating and assessing data from previous owners the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) and Shell Australia Ltd.
The company continued to spend about A$1.5 million a year in current mining areas.
Several North American companies had recently expressed interest in farming into 2,000 unexplored square kilometres of tenements held by the company, Webster said.

Shareholders in the company had indicated strongly that they preferred Western Metals retain full ownership and carry out the work itself, he said. Major shareholders are Permanent Trustee Co Ltd, NM Rothschild and Sons (Aust) Pty Ltd, Padaeng Industry PCL of Thailand and other institutions.

Following the go-ahead decision for the Kapok lead/zinc operation in the Kimberleys, Western Metals said it had made a payment on Thursday to Acacia Resources Ltd of A$2.897 million. A final payament to BHP of A$4 million plus interest was due by May 31, it said.
This would complete all outstanding obligations arising from the Cadjebut lead/zinc mine in 1994, it said.
